subject: Re: Budget gate & token levers — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Alvarez <lina@verifi-pay.com>, Tom Geller <tom.g@bankdash.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-19T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: today’s discovery — budget gate, latency targets, token pressure

Hi Lina / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Pain points we heard
- High per-call token volume from nested context (user prompts + 3rd-party metadata). Current cost is the top blocker for expanding to 1M monthly active users.
- Latency sensitivity for live support flows: p95 target ~300ms for 8k context requests.
- Lack of prefix/response caching today means repeated prompts for the same verification flows are charged repeatedly.

Goals you called out
- Prove a pilot that reduces token spend ~30–50% while keeping inference latency under 350ms p95.
- Validate batch/caching levers on a subset (authentication & disputed transactions flows) over 4–6 weeks.
- Arrive at a predictable monthly spend envelope to discuss with procurement (target ceiling: $25k/month for pilot).

Preliminary cost anchors (very rough)
- Baseline current spend (your estimate): ~$45k/month for the two flows at current volume.
- With batching + prefix/KV caching + 4-bit quantized model variant we estimate 35–45% token-cost reduction in steady state. Attached is a quick spreadsheet with scenario rows (verifipay_token_econ_v1.xlsx).

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm pilot scope: which two flows (you suggested: login verification + dispute triage) — Lina to confirm by EOD Tue.
2) Redwood to ship a 4–6 week pilot plan + SOW draft and a concise cost table for procurement — Ben/Connor will draft and send by Wed.
3) Tech sync (30m) to align instrumentation and sample payloads — Connor to propose 3 windows.

Open asks for you
- Can you confirm the pilot cap (do we have flexibility to go to $35k/month if early signal looks strong)?
- Please attach a redacted sample of your typical request payloads (PII removed) so we can size KV cache hits.

Thanks — I’ll turn this into the SOW stub and Ben will follow up on pricing.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: verifipay_token_econ_v1.xlsx

From: Lina Alvarez <lina@verifi-pay.com>

Cc: Tom Geller <tom.g@bankdash.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T17:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: today’s discovery — budget gate, latency targets, token pressure

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick answers: 
- Confirmed pilot flows: login verification + dispute triage. We can include a small subset of merchant dispute types (~10% of total disputes) for the first iteration.
- Budget: our procurement gate is firm at $25k/mo for vendor pilots — we could stretch to $30k/mo for convincing early reductions, but anything above that needs VP approval.
- Payloads: attaching a sanitized sample for each flow (will send via secure link in a follow-up because of tokenization).

One more ask: could you highlight which levers are highest impact by order (e.g., prefix caching vs batching vs model variant)? That will help us prioritize instrumentation.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Lina
Head of Product, VerifiPay
Lina.Alvarez@verifi-pay.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Connor OBrien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lina Alvarez <lina@verifi-pay.com>, Tom Geller <tom.g@bankdash.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: today’s discovery — budget gate, latency targets, token pressure

Nice summary Hannah — adding a few concrete levers and how we plan to present ROI to procurement: 

Core levers (ordered by expected near-term impact)
1) Prefix/KV caching: for verification flows where the same user or merchant metadata repeats, this can eliminate repeated prompt tokens and reduce cost by 20–35% on those hit rates. We'll instrument a hit-rate baseline in week 0.
2) Request-level batching: combine low-latency micro-batches for non-interactive pipelines (e.g., dispute triage digest) to amortize decode cost — expected 10–20% saved depending on volume shape.
3) Model quantization & runtime variant: run an int4/4-bit quantized variant for background triage and fall back to a higher-fidelity model for edge cases — expected 10–20% savings with minor quality delta.
4) Prompt refactoring / structured templates: reduce token churn via tighter templates — one-time engineering effort with steady-state savings ~5–10%.

How we’ll present ROI to procurement
- Baseline vs pilot scenario: show monthly token spend and p95 latency for each flow; emphasize net spend delta and projected run-rate breakeven.
- Include safety margin: show conservative, base, and optimistic scenarios with hit rates (5/15/30%).
- Add an ops checklist (instrumentation, rollback, fallthrough model) to reduce perceived risk.

Connor — can you draft the instrumentation list (metrics + sample logs + sample sanitized payload patterns)? I’ll assemble the cost table and SOW stub and aim to send both by Wed 10/21.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (212) 555-0112

Attachments: redwood_pilot_scope.pdf (draft)

Lina —

Perfect, thanks for confirming scope and the budget constraint. Quick commitments from our side: 
- Ben will send the SOW stub + cost-table by end of day Wed (10/21).
- Connor will propose three 30m windows for the technical sync (Thu/Fri options) and include the instrumentation checklist.
- I’ll attach the redacted sample payload link once we receive it from you; we’ll use that to run an initial KV cache estimate and update the spreadsheet assumptions.

Short answer to your ordering question: prefix/KV caching first, batching second, model variant third — we’ll validate sequencing in week 0.

If VerifiPay can sign the pilot SOW within two business days of receiving it we can target a Nov 1 pilot kick.

I’ll follow up with calendar invites once Ben/Connor send their items.

Thanks — excited to get started.

Best,
Hannah
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
